title: macOS may take Ctrl+1..9 for Mission Control, the keys that jump between tabs
notes:
src/actions.ts, the project-jump rows ship Ctrl+1..Ctrl+9 on the mac side. Mission Control's Switch to Desktop 1..9 are the same keys and come alive once you have a second Space. Where they are alive, Ctrl+2 slides you to another desktop instead of jumping to tab 2 - and project-jump is the most-pressed row in the table.

Same shape as the bug PR #23 fixed for Ctrl+Up and Ctrl+Down, which macOS took for Mission Control and Application windows. That PR wrote the rule down above the table: Ctrl with an arrow belongs to macOS. Ctrl with a digit was not checked.

Checked, and the check did not settle it. `defaults read com.apple.symbolichotkeys` holds Switch to Desktop as ids 118 upwards - but this machine's plist has been edited: ids 118..122 carry modifier 1048576, which is Cmd, not the 262144 that means Ctrl, and only desktops 1 to 5 have an entry at all. Every one reads `enabled = 0`, so nothing takes the keystroke here, and the file cannot say what a stock mac does with Ctrl+1.

So the clash cannot bite on this machine, and on a stock mac it is still an open question. The defaults stay. The rule is written above the ACTIONS table beside the one PR #23 left for the arrows, and the settings screen is the escape if the setting is ever turned on. Ctrl+Shift+1..9 for project-move looks clear either way.

If the defaults ever have to move, it cannot be the swap made for the arrows: Cmd+1..Cmd+9 is already terminal-focus on the mac side, so it needs a different family. actions.test.ts already refuses two actions on one key per screen, so a bad swap fails there rather than shipping.

https://github.com/naeemba/dashboard/issues/25
https://github.com/naeemba/dashboard/pull/23

Shipped in PR #38: the eight-line rule above the ACTIONS table, and the defaults left where they are. No key moved. The card that came out of it - a comment trail on a card, in the app and in the board command - is its own card in Todo.
